chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If the servants, when they were ignorant, paused and did not reject (the truth), they would not have been disbelievers.
ai.seo_question: What distinguishes a believer from a disbeliever in terms of handling ignorance?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between mere ignorance (jahal) and the arrogance of denial (jahd), emphasizing that intellectual humility preserves one's faith. It highlights that Kufr is often a result of stubbornly rejecting known truths rather than a lack of knowledge itself, a nuance critical in evaluating the spiritual status of the common believer. This perspective encourages seeking clarification when uncertain, rather than asserting false certainty.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If the servant, when they were ignorant (of a matter), paused and not rejected, would not have been Unbelievers (Kafirs)’.
en.sarwar: 19. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Bukayr from Zurara from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Had the servants (of Allah) when ignorant stood on hold and did not reject or deny they would not become unbelievers.’”
